open_points.subject: State 5 conventions — refusal/write atomicity
open_points.text: "A refusal is decided before the operation's first store change, so it writes nothing" and "When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay"
open_points.question: Can an operation return a refusal code after earlier store changes in the same request have already committed, or must every refusal imply no writes at all for that request?
options: All refusal codes (including `internal_error`) imply zero writes in that request
Precondition refusals imply zero writes, but `internal_error` may be returned after earlier committed changes
open_points.default_guess: Precondition refusals write nothing; `internal_error` may occur after earlier committed changes.

open_points.subject: Surface mapping of `stop_required` to MCP `internal_error`
open_points.text: "`internal_error` | the failing store change wrote nothing; changes the request made before it stay" and "`module:surface` returns it unchanged except `internal_error` and `stop_required`, which it answers as `internal_error`" plus "here, unlike any other internal error, that record was written"
open_points.question: What guarantee should callers attach to MCP `internal_error`: does it always mean the failing change wrote nothing, or can it also mean a `stop_required` path where a record was written?
options: `internal_error` at MCP level always means no write by the failing change
`internal_error` at MCP level is overloaded and may include `stop_required` cases where a record was already written
open_points.default_guess: Treat MCP `internal_error` as overloaded; caller must re-read state and not assume no writes.

open_points.subject: `get_repair_view` continuation token validity scope
open_points.text: "with a continuation token that also carries the implementation set of its first page; passed back, it pages only the NodeExecutions below that position for that set"
open_points.question: If that continuation token is later used with a different slot id or with changed paging parameters beyond size, must the call be refused, or silently continue using the token-embedded slot/set context?
options: Refuse as `invalid_request` when token context (slot/set) does not match request
Ignore request context and page strictly by token-embedded context

open_points.subject: File-port schema checking semantics (`fit_port_value` vs proof rules)
open_points.text: State 2 A05 phase 3 requires for files "both carry the same schema ... and ... the same media type", while State 5 `fit_port_value` says "for a file, the schema check is its media type against the port's"
open_points.question: For file carriage, is `value_schema` a checked contract fact at runtime fit checks, or is media type the only schema check?
options: Check both `value_schema` and media type for file ports
Ignore `value_schema` for file ports and check media type only
open_points.default_guess: At runtime fit checks, use media type only; schema equality for file ports is enforced at proof/composition time.

open_points.subject: `read_spooled_file` input fields that are 'descriptive' only
open_points.text: "its digest, size and media type only describe it — an identity naming no SpooledFile is `unknown_reference`"
open_points.question: When caller-supplied digest/size/media_type disagree with stored SpooledFile facts but lookup identity matches, must the operation refuse, or ignore those descriptive fields and return bytes?
options: Validate descriptive fields and refuse on mismatch
Ignore descriptive fields for lookup/authorization and return the bytes for the identity
open_points.default_guess: Ignore descriptive fields and return bytes for the identity; only lookup identity is authoritative.
